body:
I started smoking when I was 17.
It was something entirely different back then, a sense of rebellion, a form of independence, a means to fit in...
I would smoke every Friday when my parents were at work, it was still novel back then, but it eventually turned into an every day thing. I took the high too seriously, started looking into the psychedelic experience, the nature of reality...
It drove me crazy and I had a nervous breakdown, eventually recovering when I went away to college. I learned that I was still novice when it came to this stuff. I smoked socially and things became better for a while...
I was 20 years old when I was started using DMT and mushrooms. Life was a big party. Life wasn't so heavy back then. I was painting a lot and playing music. It was a good time....
I was arrested for possession of a cds and paraphernalia just before my 21st birthday. It's ironic that being put on probation caused me to use harder drugs.   I was seriously depressed, and started using xanax and percocet. I was a loser looking to get high on whatever I could, but eventually I finished my legal bullshit and started smoking again.
I moved out west to live with my sister and get away from my demons. The pot was great, and things were okay. I was actually sober most of the time. Traveling did me some good, and I started talking with a really cool girl... Then my brother got sick.
He was a physicist working for the government. He was exposed to some shit we still are asking questions about. Terminal cancer. Horror. Anguish. Sorrow.
It hurt me. I was smoking as much as I could to cover the pain. I started using xanax again. Every day. As much as I wanted. I didn't care. My brother passed 8 months later. I had the sense to get off the benzos. It sucked. It felt like my skeleton was trying to crawl out of my mouth. I thought I was going to die every single day. I was still smoking weed constantly.
Then my friends were killed. Drunk driving. More horror. More anguish. More sorrow. Pain. I remember drinking codeine syrup when they died. The bottle I had dulled the pain. The weed was my nurse. The codeine was my escape.
The girl I was talking to became my girlfriend over those sad months. She saved me. I would've destroyed myself if it wasn't for her. She introduced me to Ketamine. Two big fat lines, one in each nostril, astral bliss. Of all the drugs I've used, Ketamine was the most therapeutic. I remember getting in touch with my pain while swimming through the K-holes. A dream world. I remember thinking that this was what it must be like to die. Complete separation from myself. Helpless, fearless, painless. The ketamine filled the holes in my brain. It made the pain go away. It forced me to remember what it was like before I started getting fucked up.
I used weed and k for about 2 years after that. Self medication. I started seeing a councilor too. I realized that I needed to get control of my life and I made some changes. I'm no longer with that special person in the relationship sense, but she will always be important to me. I stopped using K. I stopped smoking. Sobriety took a while to get used to.
Now I stand alone without a security blanket, face to face with my demons. I stare them down. I am triumphant. I see the delusion of the dead head mentality. I see how drugs are used to keep people in control. A bowl here and there might not hurt, but needing the high to function is a reality most fail to see.
